sections.content: Very boring, difficult, complicated content. There're three weekly assignments that need to be written at least 2-3 pages. And readings for the weekly assignments are pretty long (at least 40 pages or above). And one final essay with at least 12 pages. Attendance is required for every lesson.
sections.teaching: The professor requires every single student to answer a question by calling out their names in class. And which would be a bit harsh to a college student.
sections.grading: Grading is alright with the professor graded mainly by impression. For weekly assignment, the TA didn't give out the grade on time to let you know how your performance for the past assignments was before submitting the new one.
sections.workload: The workload is alright; just don't pack your weekly assignment at the final three weeks before the semester ends since it doesn't have a one full week to complete it instead. And the professor will only reveal the final essay topic on the last lesson.

sections.content: Most of the time spent during class, you'd be hearing students presenting rather than him doing the lecture. He might make a comment or two, but not much is taught. He sometimes pulls some readings in word documents out of nowhere. Not much content from him, but rather from other students and discussions.
sections.teaching: Still, a good prof. He can be stubborn sometimes (in a good way), but definitely encourages you to speak up (increasingly a rarity nowadays).
sections.grading: Excellent. Been gaming during most lectures and did almost zero readings. Attend all lectures, and you'll get a safe B range.
sections.workload: Extremely low workload. Simply do your part of the presentation (throughout a tutorial time) and you can sit back and do your own stuff from then on.

sections.content: Content ok, it basically has 3-4 lessons for the introduction of democracy and the concept of democracy. and the remaining lessons are for students' presentations. not many teaching at all i think.
sections.teaching: Professor will always raise some critical questions for us to think. but he is willing to answer the questions we proposed. however i think it is a bit boring, and because of the duration of the whole lesson, it lasts for 3 hours (start from 1200 and end at 1450), it is very easy for people to fall asleep.
sections.grading: very nice overall. didn't pay much effort into it but still can get a B- for the group presentation and essay paper. no attendance is needed
sections.workload: very light workload. no midterm and final. no quiz and never take attendance (but the class size is very small and so if you don't come to the prof maybe remember) only one huge presentation which requires to undergo 30~40 mins and one paper after the presentation and have the same topic of it. So compare to other sosc course, the workload is very light.
